after.authors: Wakoli, D. M.; Rotich, B.; Mbugua, E.; Van Hulle, S.; Kipkoech, J.; Abel, L.; Katairo, T.; Kimachas, E.; Wesolowski, A.; Conrad, M.; Menya, D.; OMeara, W. P.
after.abstract: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) is an important malaria prevention strategy used widely in areas of West Africa with highly seasonal transmission. Monthly administration of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (SPAQ) to young children during the high-transmission season substantially reduces malaria morbidity and mortality. SMC has recently been introduced in northern Kenya, where pastoralist communities experience intense malaria transmission. However, implementation in this setting presents unique challenges, including population mobility, vast distances, dispersed settlements, and high levels of parasite resistance to SP in parts of the region. Effective surveillance is needed to identify gaps in SMC delivery and uptake and to monitor threats to program effectiveness. We implemented an innovative sentinel-site surveillance approach in which every malaria case among SMC-eligible children at selected health facilities was investigated to identify gaps in SMC delivery, uptake, and effectiveness. We also assessed the prevalence of parasite alleles associated with SP and AQ resistance and examined their relationship with SMC uptake. Household travel was substantially more common than caregiver refusal among reported reasons for missing an SMC cycle. More than one-third of children presenting with malaria had missed their most recent SMC cycle, while 15% were within a few days of receiving the next scheduled cycle. The prevalence of SP resistance mutations was considerably lower than reported in other parts of East Africa: only 13.4% of infections carried the quintuple mutant haplotype IRNI/GEAA (PfDHFR 51I, 59R, 108N, PfDHPS 437G, 540E) associated with high level resistance to SP. However, the prevalence of resistance-associated mutations was higher among children who had recently received SMC. The allele associated with reduced susceptibility to AQ was not detected. Sentinel surveillance identified geographic and implementation gaps in real time, allowing program managers to target SMC distribution and community sensitization. Although the prevalence of resistance-associated mutations that could threaten SPAQ effectiveness was low, evidence of intrahost selection among children who had received SMC suggests that continued molecular surveillance will be important as SMC is scaled up in northern Kenya. This sentinel surveillance approach provides a practical framework for monitoring SMC implementation in remote, highly mobile populations while simultaneously tracking emerging threats to SPAQ effectiveness.

after.authors: SAMWEL, R.; Barabona, G.; Kimwela, H.; Samji, S.; Meza, W.; Abeid, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Aga Khan Hospital Dar es Salaam
after.abstract: Background About 0.07% to 8% of parturients will require intensive care unit (ICU) admission during pregnancy, childbirth or puerperium, with great regional variations. When this occurs, it increases morbidity, mortality, long-term physical and psychological sequelae as well as cost. This study sought to examine a five-year admission rate, indications and outcomes of parturients with severe morbidities admitted in the ICU at a tertiary referral facility and teaching hospital in Tanzania. Methodology A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at Muhimbili National Hospital in Dar es Salaam city that included all women who were admitted to the obstetric ICU between 2019 and 2023. Data were retrospectively collected using a pre-tested checklist from all 1526 obstetric ICU admissions, out of 29391 obstetric unit admissions, during the study period. Sources of data were both case files and electronic registries in the ICU and labour ward. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with maternal mortality, with results presented as adjusted odds ratios (aOR) while indications of ICU admission and maternal outcomes were presented descriptively by using frequencies and tables. Results Out of 29391 obstetric unit admissions, 1526 required ICU, resulting into obstetric ICU admission rate of 5.2%. Hypertensive disorders were the leading cause of admission (73.7%) followed by obstetric haemorrhages (15%). Frequent ICU interventions included; mechanical ventilation (50%), anticonvulsants (26%), blood transfusion (15%), inotropes (4.2%), and dialysis (3.5%). Maternal fatality rate was 14%. In multivariable regression analysis, vaginal delivery was associated with 47% higher odds of mortality compared to caesarean section (aOR 1.47, 95% CI 1.03-2.11, p=0.036). A moderate ICU stay of 3-4 days showed a 91% protective effect relative to stays of [≤]2 days (aOR 0.09, P < 0.001). 5-7day stays were also protective (aOR 0.32, p=0.006). Anticonvulsant use was strongly protective against mortality (aOR 0.02, p < 0.001). Conclusion This five years review of obstetric ICU admissions (2019-2023) showed that, approximately one in 20 obstetric patients required critical care, with one in seven of ICU admissions resulting in maternal death. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy accounted for majority of ICU admissions, and deaths occurred predominantly during the early phase of critical care. These findings underscore the need to strengthen antenatal risk identification, optimise referral and emergency obstetric care, ensure timely magnesium sulphate administration, and establish obstetric high dependency units to facilitate earlier interventions. Such measures could reduce the burden on ICUs while improving maternal outcomes.

after.abstract: Background Non-ventilator-associated hospital-acquired pneumonia (nv-HAP) diagnosis is imprecise; chest x-rays (CXR) lack detail and sputum culture delays targeted prescribing. However, the evidence base to support diagnostic improvement is sparse. We assessed the feasibility of a trial of low-dose thoracic CT and rapid molecular testing of sputum. Methods HAP-FAST was a UK NIHR funded, open-label pilot sequential multiple assignment randomised trial with qualitative and costing substudies in four UK hospitals (ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT05483309). Using research without prior consent (RWPC) and site-stratified web-based randomisation, clinicians allocated adults with suspected nv-HAP (excluding pregnancy and palliation), before their second antibiotic dose, 1:1 to CT or CXR; participants subsequently treated for nv-HAP with sputum available underwent another 1:1 randomisation to BIOFIRE(R) FILMARRAY(R) Pneumonia plus Panel (FAPP) with standard microbiology or standard microbiology alone . Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, consent, intervention delivery and data completeness through 90 days. Adverse events were not systematically collected. Analyses were intention-to-treat and descriptive. Results Between June 2023 and March 2024, 220 adults were randomised at stage-1 (109 CT; 111 CXR), reaching target three months early. Of 154/220 (70.0%) subsequently managed as nv-HAP, 92/154 (59.7%) could not produce sputum. 62/154 (40.3%; 28.2% of stage-1) were randomised to stage-2: 31 FAPP and 31 no-FAPP. Allocated imaging was recorded for 75/109 (68.8%) CT and 99/111 (89.2%) CXR participants; 6/31(19.4%) FAPP tests were not completed. Consent for follow-up was obtained for 142/220 (64.5%). Protocol-defined clinical cure was assessable in 1/220 participants. The day-90 resource-use questionnaire was returned by 55/110 participants (50.0%). Qualitative findings supported RWPC but identified needs for staged communication, lower-burden follow-up and improved diagnostic pathways. Excess bed days and readmissions drove costs but data capture requires refinement. Conclusions A definitive trial is plausible only with enhanced RWPC, diagnostic delivery and follow-up pathways, improved sputum procedures, stewardship-aligned outcomes and routine economic data capture.

after.abstract: Background: Over 3.5 million US men are living with prostate cancer (PCa). Certain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are carcinogenic and impair cardiometabolic health. Due to comorbidities and treatment, men with PCa may be uniquely susceptible to PFAS. Objectives: To develop and validate a model for drinking water perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), and perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), and study associations of each PFAS with all-cause, PCa, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in PCa survivors. Methods: We conducted a cohort study of 51,289 men with PCa diagnosed from 2006 to 2017 and followed through 2024 from the New Jersey (NJ) cancer registry. PFAS monitoring data (n=26,161 results) were obtained from NJ government evaluations and Community Water Systems (CWS) compliance reports and were used to estimate PFAS concentrations using a two-phase XGBoost model with 67 predictors of PFAS contamination across 566 CWS. PFAS predictions between 2006-2024 were linked to participant address histories. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated from Cox models with sociodemographic, clinical and time-varying neighborhood covariates. Results: There were 19,749 deaths, including 3,778 PCa deaths, and 4,972 CVD deaths over 466,843 person-years. Higher PFOA exposure was associated with all-cause mortality in certain quintiles (aHRQ2vsQ1: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.07-1.12; aHRQ3vsQ1: 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11) and with CVD mortality (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.01-1.24). Higher PFNA exposure was suggestively associated with all-cause mortality (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.22, 95% CI: 0.98-1.50) and PCa mortality (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.42, 95% CI: 0.96-2.10). Associations were strengthened when applying five-year lags. For example, higher PFOA (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.06-1.25), PFOS (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.07-1.25) and PFNA (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.06-2.31) were associated with higher all-cause mortality. Discussion: Exposure to CWS-level PFAS was associated with higher mortality in PCa survivors. Replication is needed to confirm findings.

after.title: Preprint: Influenza Vaccination and Disease Severity Among Older Adults Hospitalized with Influenza in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study, 2016-2024
after.authors: Abou Chakra, C. N.; Diallo, A. B.; Some, A.; Pitel, B.; Bricout, H.; EL GUERCHE-SEBLAIN, C.; Chauvel, C.; Nunes, M.
after.abstract: Objective Seasonal influenza remains a major cause of severe morbidity and mortality among older adults, despite vaccine availability. We assessed whether influenza vaccination was associated with reduced disease severity among adults aged 65 years or more hospitalized with influenza in France. Methods and Analysis We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults aged 65 years or more hospitalized with confirmed influenza (ICD-10 codes: J09 or J10) between October 2016 and December 2024 were included, excluding 2020-2021. Vaccination status was identified from reimbursed community pharmacy dispensing records. Entropy balancing was used to balance sociodemographic characteristics, chronic conditions pneumococcal vaccination, and COVID-19 vaccination. Weighted regression models estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), intensive care unit (ICU) admission, in-hospital death, and a composite severe outcome. Multistate survival models assessed transitions specific hazard ratios (HR) between hospitalization, ICU, discharge, and in-hospital death. Results Among 132,443 influenza-associated hospitalizations, 72,852 (55%) occurred among vaccinated patients and 59,591 (45%) among unvaccinated patients. Vaccinated patients were older (mean age, 82.3 vs 79.3 years). IMV occurred in 2128 vaccinated (2.9%) and 2544 unvaccinated (4.3%) hospitalizations (aRR, 0.88; 95%CI: 0.83 to 0.93). In-hospital death occurred in 6300 (8.6%) and 4952 (8.3%), respectively (aRR, 0.90; 95%CI: 0.87 to 0.93). Vaccination was also associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (aRR, 0.96; 95%CI: 0.94 to 0.98), but not ICU admission (aRR, 0.99; 95%CI: 0.96 to 1.01). Among patients admitted to ICU, vaccination was associated with a lower hazard of death (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.85; 95%CI: 0.78 to 0.92) and a 2-day reduction in the median time to discharge. Conclusion In this nationwide cohort study, influenza vaccination was associated with lower risks of IMV and in-hospital death among older adults hospitalized with influenza. These findings are consistent with possible attenuation of disease severity and support efforts to improve influenza vaccination among older adults.

after.authors: Makowski, C.; Bansal, D.; Moorman, B.; Garcia, K.; Ziemer, L.; Linkersdorfer, J.; Barch, D.; Hagan, K.; Rhee, K. E.; Adise, S.
after.abstract: Eating disorders (EDs) are serious psychiatric conditions that typically onset during adolescence and are often marked by a chronic and severe illness course. Capturing ED symptoms as they emerge is critical for charting risk markers and associated outcomes to inform early intervention and treatment efforts. The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD(R)) Study is one such key study that could accelerate these efforts, but has been limited to date by a lack of clear, clinically informed definitions capturing youth at risk for ED-related concerns. The current manuscript aims to address this gap by defining ED symptom indices (EDSI) with a reproducible framework developed in collaboration with ED researchers and clinicians to identify youth with patterns of ED symptoms and behaviors that approximate subthreshold and diagnostic-like presentations. We describe item-level definitions and decision rules used to construct the EDSI, which include symptom indices of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and other specified feeding or eating disorders. We then compare youth meeting EDSI criteria with those identified by existing ED categorical definitions in ABCD Study data releases. By providing transparent definitions and analytical tools for identifying youth with potentially clinically meaningful ED behaviors, the EDSI framework aims to facilitate more reproducible and interpretable research related to EDs using the ABCD Study dataset, while also providing a structure to examine the emergence, persistence, and change of ED-like symptoms longitudinally across adolescence and into young adulthood in future research.

after.authors: Amugi, G.; Baah, E. M.; Yankey, H.; Kwarkye, I.; Mensah, P.; Jean Claude, K.; Jubin, D.; Kaba Akoriyea, S.; Bekoe, F. A.; Laryea, D.; Abdul-Tawab, A.; Arthur, J.; Kutsoati, S.; Oliver-Commey, J.; Mohammed, N. T.
after.abstract: Mpox re-emerged as a global public health concern in 2022, and the Western Region of Ghana became the epicentre of the countrys largest recorded outbreak in 2025. Ahead of a sub-national vaccination campaign launched in October 2025, no study had examined the determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the region using a theoretically grounded framework. This study determined the sociodemographic and Health Belief Model-based determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Western Region, Ghana. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 580 adults in six purposively selected peri-urban areas and their surrounding communities between July and August 2025, before the vaccination campaign began. Vaccine acceptance was measured as a three-category outcome (accept, hesitant, refuse) and analysed using chi square tests and multinomial logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, Health Belief Model constructs, and peri-urban area. Overall, 75.7% of respondents were willing to accept the vaccine, 12.9% were hesitant and 11.4% would refuse. Perceived vaccine safety was the strongest determinant: respondents who considered the vaccine very safe had markedly lower adjusted odds of hesitancy (adjusted odds ratio 0.02, 95% confidence interval 0.00-0.12) and refusal (0.03, 0.01-0.13) than those who considered it unsafe. Uncertainty about vaccine effectiveness was associated with hesitancy (9.83, 1.95-49.50), and belief in its effectiveness with lower odds of refusal (0.22, 0.06-0.86). Higher educational attainment was associated with lower odds of hesitancy, being a student or employed with lower odds of refusal, and acceptance differed be 1 tween peri-urban areas (55.1% to 95.6%). Knowledge of mpox transmission was associated with acceptance in bivariate analysis (p < 0.001) but not after adjustment. Risk communication that addresses vaccine safety and effectiveness, rather than generic disease-awareness messaging alone, is likely to be most effec tive in improving mpox vaccine acceptance in this population, with unemployed and less-educated residents warranting targeting. As a pre-campaign baseline collected during an active outbreak, these findings can inform the vaccination response in the Western Region and preparedness in comparable peri-urban West African settings.

after.authors: Dayma, K.; Newton, C.; Kawzowicz, M.; Patel, P.; Curl, R.; Ogden, K.
after.abstract: Background. FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for pulmonary embolism (PE) detection has been widely used; however, its performance has not been analyzed for subgroups, clinical sites, and temporal stability. Methods. This retrospective, six-site health system study evaluated the Aidoc BriefCase PE triage model (K190072) across 14,736 CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) examinations between July 2023 and March 2026. Reference-standard PE characteristic labels were extracted from radiology reports using a zero-shot LLM pipeline validated against a radiologist-annotated 600 reports ({kappa} =0.98). Model performance was evaluated across demographics, embolus characteristics, and site. Temporal behavior was evaluated on operating point by logistic regression, with and without site adjustment, and by segmented regression. Results. PE was present in 1,402/14,736 examinations (9.5%). Overall sensitivity was 64.1% (95% CI, 61.5-66.6%), specificity 98.8% (95% CI, 98.6-99.0%), compared with 93% sensitivity and 93.7% specificity in the FDA 510(k) summary. Sensitivity fell with peripherality (central 88.6%, lobar or segmental 63.1%, subsegmental 33.3%) and with chronicity (acute 65.5%, chronic 57.4%). Sensitivity differed significantly between the two highest-volume sites, 68.7% and 55.7% (P < .001), with CT scanner as the only variable different between the two sites. The false-positive rate fell 40% per year (P<.001) at a similar rate at two sites, while sensitivity fell 15% per year at site A (P<.036), from 72.5% to 65.0% between two halves of the study period. The manufacturer did not report model updates or threshold changes during the study period. Conclusions. Deployed sensitivity was substantially below the cleared benchmark and varied 13 points by site. The gradual shift in high specificity at the cost of low sensitivity, either from data drift or threshold change, either not monitored or not documented by the manufacturer, highlights the importance of independent continuous post-market monitoring.

Model performance was evaluated across demographics, embolus characteristics, and site. Deployed sensitivity was substantially below the cleared benchmark and varied 13 points by site. after.title: Preprint: A National Survey Exploring Dementia Care Provision in Social Care in England
after.authors: Darby, A.; Durkin, C.; Chapman, H.; Kelsey, O.; Kenten, C.; Banerjee, S.; Birks, Y.; Cooper, C.
after.abstract: Context: Dementia is associated with significant use of social care, yet we know little about how providers respond to increasing demand and policy ambitions to deliver more care in community settings. Objective: To examine dementia care provision, workforce training, service integration, and perceived challenges among care homes and home care agencies in England. Methods: We conducted a mixed methods co-designed survey of care home and home care agency managers across five geographically diverse English regions, exploring: training, service delivery, relationships with other services, and future priorities. We analysed data descriptively and free-text responses using qualitative content analysis. Findings: We received valid responses from 42 home care agencies and 47 care home managers, who estimated around one third of home care clients, and most care home residents, had significant cognitive impairment. Most care homes held regular multidisciplinary meetings (29/40, 72.5%). Home care managers described positive collaborations with health and other social care services, but also difficulties accessing support and concerns about undervaluation of care workforce skills within multidisciplinary care. Across both settings, frequently reported challenges included: increasing care complexity, behaviours that challenge, recruitment, retention and financial constraints. In home care settings, difficulties working in partnership with families were cited as reasons for care breakdown. Most organisations provided dementia-specific training, identifying communication, behavioural support, de-escalation, safeguarding, and working with families as unmet training needs. Limitations: Findings are probably limited by response and desirability bias; we did not triangulate findings with objective data. Implications: As policy shifts care to community settings, investment in social care workforce development, specialist support and integrated pathways are essential for sustainable high quality dementia care. Increased funding, improved training, stronger career pathways, and greater recognition of care workers were identified as priorities for improving dementia care.

after.abstract: Background: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is a low-cost, radiation-free triage tool but lacks standardized acquisition protocols for tuberculosis (TB). We developed and evaluated a streamlined symmetric POCUS protocol for pulmonary TB in a high-burden setting. Methods: Ugandan participants aged [≥]13 years with confirmed pulmonary TB, household TB exposure, or a non-TB respiratory condition underwent an 18-position POCUS examination (12 lung zones and 6 pre-established extrapulmonary positions). Random Forest classifiers using prespecified pathologic features were developed in a fixed stratified 75/25 training/holdout split. All symmetric 2-, 4-, and 6-zone combinations were evaluated in training data. The best protocol of each size was locked and tested in the holdout set. Results: Among 318 analyzed participants, 118 (37.1%) had pulmonary TB and 200 were TB-negative, including 102 with other respiratory conditions (ORC). The model-selected 6-zone protocol comprised bilateral anterior-superior, lateral-superior, and posterior-superior lung zones. For TB versus all TB-negative participants, the AUCs for the 6-zone, 12-zone, and 18-position protocols were 0.82 (95% CI, 0.73-0.92), 0.81 (0.70--0.92), and 0.81 (0.71--0.91), respectively (all P > 0.76). For TB versus ORC, AUCs were 0.81 (0.70--0.91), 0.85 (0.76--0.93), and 0.85 (0.76--0.94), respectively (all P > 0.45). The 2-zone protocol had a lower AUC than the 6-zone protocol for TB versus all TB-negative participants (P = 0.004). Shred sign, consolidation, and B-lines with irregular pleura were the strongest TB-associated findings. Conclusions: A fixed 6-zone lung POCUS examination showed similar discrimination for TB to more comprehensive 12-lung-zone and 18-position protocols. This supports a simpler, scalable approach to TB triage

after.title: Preprint: How Many Time-Critical Emergencies? A Population-Based National Estimate of Attended Events per 100,000 US Residents
after.authors: Haight, D.; Nisbet, K. A.; Li, S.
after.abstract: Objectives. To estimate how many time-critical emergencies fire and emergency medical services (EMS) crews attend each year per 100,000 US residents. We counted events in which a crew reached a living patient or a trapped person whose outcome plausibly depends on how soon effective treatment starts. Methods. For 30 medical conditions, we took annual counts from US registries and datasets, or multiplied a national incidence count by the share of patients EMS attended. A condition was Tier A when a published study linked a measured delay, from minutes to a few hours, to death or major disability. Conditions whose time sensitivity rests on guidelines or expert consensus were Tier B. Fire and rescue events came from twelve months of National Emergency Response Information System public data, scaled to national totals. We removed double counting between conditions. Results. Crews attended an estimated 589 time-critical events per 100,000 residents a year (494 to 697 with every condition at its low or high value), equal to 4.3% of 9-1-1 EMS activations. Medical conditions accounted for 583 after removing overlap. Of these, 350 were Tier A, led by ischemic stroke (120.2) and EMS-treated cardiac arrest (78.7). Opioid overdose (123.4) led the 233 Tier B events. Those three conditions made up 55% of the medical total. Fire and rescue events added 6. Conclusions. At national rates, a US community of 100,000 can expect its fire and EMS crews to attend about 589 events a year in which time to treatment may change the outcome. That is roughly 11 a week, nearly all of them medical. The count measures how often response time can matter in the events crews attend, and it gives a denominator for valuing a faster response.

after.title: Preprint: Unraveling the genetic architecture of the human mammillary bodies
after.authors: Imtiaz, M. A.; Xu, P.; Estrada, S.; Saleh, M. M.; Racine, I. S.; Liu, D.; Breteler, M. M. B.; Aziz, N. A.
after.abstract: The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univariate GWAS identified 34 genomic loci associated with mammillary body volume, including 26 novel loci, with 20 loci showing replication in the Rhineland Study. Meta-analysis across both cohorts (N = 42,924) identified 44 associated loci, of which 35 were novel. Multivariate GWAS of hypothalamic subregions identified 55 loci, including 40 novel associations. Integrative cross-omics analyses identified MEI1 and CAPZA1 as key molecular candidates, with genetically regulated MEI1 expression and circulating CAPZA1 protein levels partially mediating genetic effects on mammillary body volume. Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization analyses further revealed a bidirectional relationship between mammillary body volume and major depressive disorder. Together, our findings elucidate the genetic architecture of mammillary body volume and its relation to mental disorders.

after.authors: Jafari, M.; Moradi, N.; Abdolahi, H.; Keshaei, F.
after.abstract: Abstract Background: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection remains highly prevalent in Iran, where high antibiotic resistance can limit eradication efficacy. Saccharomyces boulardii (S. boulardii) may improve eradication and treatment tolerability, although evidence remains inconsistent. This trial evaluated adjunctive S. boulardii in a high-prevalence, high-resistance setting. Methods: In this randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 218 H. pylori-positive adults received 14 days of PPI, bismuth, amoxicillin, and clarithromycin (P-BAC) plus either S. boulardii (250 mg twice daily) or placebo. The primary outcome was H. pylori eradication assessed 30 days after treatment by stool antigen testing, analyzed by intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) principles. Treatment-related adverse events were secondary outcomes. Trial registration: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials, IRCT20230827059280N1. Results: In the PP analysis, eradication was lower with S. boulardii than placebo (65.0% vs. 76.5%; RR = 0.849, 95% CI: 0.709-1.018), with a similar pattern in the ITT analysis (59.6% vs. 68.8%; RR = 0.867, 95% CI: 0.710-1.058). Neither analysis showed a statistically significant difference. Overall adverse events were significantly less frequent with S. boulardii (44.0% vs. 68.4%; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.497-0.834; P < 0.001), with lower rates of bloating (4.0% vs. 23.5%; adjusted P < 0.001) and epigastric pain (4.0% vs. 14.3%; adjusted P = 0.041). Conclusion: Adjunctive S. boulardii did not significantly improve H. pylori eradication with 14-day P-BAC therapy. However, it significantly reduced adverse events, particularly bloating and epigastric pain. Further multicenter trials incorporating individualized susceptibility testing are warranted.

after.title: Preprint: Measuring community building in group antenatal care: Evidence from a randomized trial in Malawi
after.authors: Batchelder, A.; Hanson, G. C.; Kapito, E.; Chirwa, E.; Patil, C. L.; Glass, N.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing
after.abstract: Improving the quality of antenatal care is essential for reducing persistently high maternal and neonatal mortality in Malawi. Group antenatal care has demonstrated improvements in quality, satisfaction, health behaviors, and outcomes. However, the impact of community building, one of the models core components, has not previously been quantitatively assessed. This study examined the measurement properties of two community building measures, assessed the impact of group antenatal care on these measures, and explored their potential role as mediators of health outcomes. This secondary analysis used quantitative data from the parent study testing the effectiveness of group antenatal care at seven clinics in Blantyre District, Malawi. The Perinatal Peer Support Scale and the Provider Connectedness subscale of the Pregnancy Related Empowerment Scale were used to measure community building and were validated using factor analyses. Results supported a two-factor structure for perinatal peer support (relational support and peer network) and a unidimensional structure for provider connectedness. Using generalized linear modeling, we found that participation in group antenatal care was associated with significantly stronger community building across all measures when compared to usual individual antenatal care. Women in group antenatal care demonstrated higher relational support score, peer network, and provider connectedness scores compared with women in individual antenatal care (p < 0.001). However, we found no evidence that community building had direct or indirect (mediating) effects on maternal psychological distress or infant birthweight. This study strengthens the evidence base for group antenatal care by validating measures of community building and showing that relational support, peer networks, and provider connectedness are important benefits of participation. Although community building did not mediate the outcomes examined here, the findings highlight the need to further test of theoretical pathways linking group antenatal care to maternal and child health outcomes.

after.abstract: Kidney disease is a rapidly growing global health concern, tightly linked to cardiovascular and metabolic disease within the recently defined cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Routine clinical assessment of kidney function primarily relies on creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rates (eGFRcr) which can be affected by non-renal factors and declines only after substantial kidney damage. Using data from the MetaCardis study (N=1,723), we derived metabolomic kidney function gaps (mKFGs)-the difference between metabolome-predicted eGFRcr and measured eGFRcr. A physiology-guided feature-selection strategy - anchored on three cardiometabolic markers (haemoglobin, albumin and the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio) that associate with mKFGs but not with eGFRcr - yielded compact sex-stratified metabolite panels (40-98 out of 1,514 metabolites) that tracked cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk. Machine-Learning models revealed distinct metabolic signatures, including biomarkers of meat consumption and androgens, highlighting potential sex-specific pathways linked to CKM health. External validation in the general-population Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (N=9,958) and German Chronic Kidney Disease Study (N=5,113) cohorts revealed that mKFGs added incremental predictive value for future CKM events and all-cause mortality beyond eGFRcr and established risk equations. Our findings open new avenues for personalised risk stratification for CKM disease progression and targeted interventions based on metabolically defined kidney health.

Machine-Learning models revealed distinct metabolic signatures, including biomarkers of meat consumption and androgens, highlighting potential sex-specific pathways linked to CKM health. after.abstract: Alternative polyadenylation contributes extensively to transcript diversification and is particularly prominent during neuronal differentiation; however, its contribution to monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders remains incompletely understood. CSTF2 encodes an RNA-binding subunit of the cleavage stimulation factor complex and has previously been associated with X-linked intellectual disability through a single Asp50Ala missense variant with increased RNA-binding activity. Here, we identify seven rare CSTF2 variants in ten hemizygous male probands with intellectual disability, global developmental delay and/or autism spectrum disorder, including missense, nonsense, splice-site, and frameshift variants. Functional analysis of selected variants using RNA sequencing and 3'-end-proximal sequencing in CSTF2-depleted cells identified Phe19Leu, Gln543ter, Leu555Ser as strongly functionally impairing variants. These variants predominantly reduced usage of intronic polyadenylation sites while increasing usage of downstream sites within terminal 3'UTRs. Suppressed intronic sites were enriched for GU-rich sequence elements, were more evolutionarily conserved, and showed higher predicted polyadenylation-site strength, consistent with preferential impairment of CSTF2-dependent polyadenylation. In contrast, the previously reported Asp50Ala variant produced an opposing pattern, with preferential activation of intronic polyadenylation sites, consistent with its increased RNA-binding activity. These findings indicate that both reduced and increased CSTF2 activity disrupt the balance of polyadenylation-site usage and can result in neurodevelopmental disorder. Our data provide genetic and functional support for CSTF2 as an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder gene, identify inactivating CSTF2 variants as a disease mechanism, and implicate dysregulation of intronic polyadenylation in human intellectual disability.

after.authors: Diouf, I.; Sambou Cissokho, M. J.; Fall, P.; Beye Gueye, A.; Doucoure, E.; Gaye, A. T.
after.abstract: Background. Malaria transmission in Senegal is seasonal and spatially heterogeneous, but the consistency of dynamical malaria models with routine surveillance has rarely been tested with monthly subnational data. Methods. We analysed monthly confirmed cases from the National Malaria Control Programme (PNLP) regional database (14 regions, 2009-2025) and reports of the 79 health districts (2016-2025). Ten bias-adjusted NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 models (1995-2014; SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 to 2100) were evaluated against CHIRPS rainfall; VECTRI was driven by MRI-ESM2-0, the model closest to the ensemble median change. Results. National incidence averaged 24.5 cases per 1,000 per year without trend over 2009-2024, but increased in Kedougou, Kolda and Tambacounda, which reported 58.7 % of cases for 11.3 % of the population. The test positivity rate (TPR) decreased from 22.5 % in 2016 to 16.2 % in 2024. Based on the seasonal centre of gravity, observed cases lagged the entomological inoculation rate (EIR) simulated by VECTRI by 1.06 months (95 % CI 0.88-1.23) and the lag was positive in 13 of 14 regions, but the regional differences in timing were not reproduced. Across 45 departments, the simulated EIR was correlated with the TPR (Spearman {rho} = 0.67, 95 % CI 0.47-0.79). In 2025, confirmed cases decreased by 55.7 % in the 34 districts of the long-lasting insecticidal net (LLIN) mass campaign against 9.7 % elsewhere. Under SSP5-8.5 in 2081-2100, the models projected +4.6 {degrees}C and -32 % annual rainfall, and the simulated EIR decreased by 35 % (p < 0.001). Conclusions. VECTRI driven by bias-adjusted CMIP6 climate reproduces the timing of the malaria season and the gradient of transmission intensity in Senegal, but not the regional differences in timing. The TPR is a population-free indicator for model evaluation. Seasonal malaria chemoprevention calendars should account for the regional timing documented here; the projected changes in timing are small.

after.authors: Bharadwaj, S.; Guang, Z.; Clark, L. A.; Callaway, J. P.; Li, Z.; Suhr, C. L.; Lucas, S. N.; Serafini, C.; Garcia-Nuno, J.; Wolner, Z.; Khan, M. K.; Thomas, S. N.; Robles, F. E.
after.abstract: Skin cancer is the most common malignancy in the United States. The gold standard for diagnosis of skin cancer is histopathological analysis via tissue biopsy. However, identifying which lesions to biopsy remains a significant clinical challenge, particularly at early stages of disease. In this work, we present a volumetric quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) probe, a highly maneuverable, handheld imaging system capable of providing high-resolution, 3D visualization of the skin microstructure. We show the probe is capable of visualizing the dynamic, layered microstructure of the epidermis and the top of the dermis across all Fitzpatrick skin types in human skin in vivo. The easy maneuverability of the probe is highlighted by imaging anatomically challenging areas typically hard to reach for bulkier systems. Finally, we present additional case studies in ex vivo murine models and in vivo human nevi that further illustrate the potential clinical applications of the volumetric handheld probe. These results establish a low-cost, easy to use, high-resolution, compact system that combines the strengths of its predecessors -- the excellent maneuverability of the widely-used dermatoscopes and 3D, high-resolution imaging of prior bulkier systems -- to improve screening of dermatological lesions at the bedside.

after.authors: Shitara, S.; Harada, A.; Tanaka-Mizuno, S.; Takashima, N.; Fujii, T.; Arima, H.; Miyamatsu, N.; Urushitani, M.; Nozaki, K.; Miura, K.; Yoshida, K.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Shiga University of Medical Science, Shiga, Japan
after.abstract: Background: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) have contrasting epidemiological characteristics, including sex-specific incidence. However, their overall contribution to sex differences in hemorrhagic stroke remains unclear because they are generally evaluated separately. We examined the sex-specific epidemiology of hemorrhagic stroke by integrating ICH and SAH. Methods: We analyzed first-ever ICH and SAH events recorded from 2011 through 2015 in the Shiga Stroke and Heart Attack Registry, a population-based registry covering approximately 1.4 million residents in Japan. Age-specific and age-adjusted incidence rates were calculated by sex and stroke subtype using direct standardization to the 2015 Japanese Census population. Results: Among 4,517 patients with hemorrhagic stroke, 3,461 (76.6%) had ICH and 1,056 (23.4%) had SAH. The age-adjusted incidence of ICH was higher in men than in women (61.2 vs 49.8 per 100,000 person-years), whereas SAH incidence was more than twice as high in women as in men (22.4 vs 10.4 per 100,000 person-years). Despite these opposing patterns, the age-adjusted incidence of hemorrhagic stroke was nearly identical between men and women (71.6 vs 72.2 per 100,000 person-years). ICH accounted for a greater share of the overall incidence among men, whereas SAH accounted for a greater share among women. Conclusions: Despite marked subtype-specific sex differences, the overall incidence of hemorrhagic stroke was similar between women and men. These findings demonstrate that substantial sex differences in individual subtypes may be offset when ICH and SAH are considered together, highlighting the value of an integrated population-level perspective in evaluating sex disparities in hemorrhagic stroke.

after.title: Preprint: The Evolving Role of Telehealth in Routine Health Care Delivery Among US Adults, 2022-2024
after.authors: Wang, S.; Lin, W.; Ge, L.
after.abstract: Background: Telehealth use expanded rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic, but its role following the end of the public health emergency (PHE) remains incompletely understood. This study examined changes in telehealth utilization among US adults between 2022 and 2024, characteristics associated with use, and changes in self-reported reasons for using telehealth to understand its evolving role. Methods: This serial cross-sectional study analyzed nationally representative data from 13 141 US adults participating in the Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) in 2022, during the COVID-19 PHE, and 2024, after the PHE ended. Survey-weighted analyses were used to estimate telehealth utilization and self-reported reasons for use. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to examine changes between survey cycles and sociodemographic and health-related characteristics associated with telehealth utilization. Multiple imputation was used to address missing data. Results: Telehealth utilization declined from 39.3% in 2022 to 34.5% in 2024; after adjustment for sociodemographic and health-related characteristics, the odds of telehealth use were significantly lower in 2024 than in 2022 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Telehealth utilization differed across population groups. Higher odds of use were observed among adults aged 35 to 49 years (aOR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.19-1.82), those with a college degree or higher (aOR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.31-2.86), those with diagnosed depression or anxiety (aOR, 2.86; 95% CI, 2.46-3.33), those with a history of cancer (aOR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.15-1.69), and insured adults (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.04). All self-reported reasons for telehealth use declined between 2022 and 2024. Infection avoidance decreased from 50.2% to 19.1% and provider recommendation or requirement from 72.8% to 47.2%, whereas convenience showed a smaller decline from 65.6% to 56.2% and became the leading reported reason for telehealth use in 2024. Conclusions: Telehealth utilization declined between 2022 and 2024, while the relative persistence of convenience as a reason for use suggests a shift away from pandemic-driven demand toward more selective integration into routine health care. Differences in utilization across population groups suggest that telehealth may address some barriers to conventional care while access remains uneven. These findings highlight the evolving role of telehealth after the COVID-19 PHE and the importance of supporting its appropriate and equitable integration into routine care.

after.authors: Khan, A.; Kulkarni, S.; Lai, S.-L.; Wang, X.; Farber, I.; Kugener, G.; Pal, A.; Volpi, S.; Zohar, O.; Chen, C.-S.; Yeung-Levy, S.; Brat, G.
after.abstract: Purpose: Objective assessment of open surgical skills remains limited by expert availability. Machine learning (ML)-based hand keypoint detection offers potential for automated, on-demand assessment, but performance in accessible browser-based recording environments (laptop-webcam video recorded in a web browser) is unknown. We hypothesized that browser-based recordings would achieve acceptable keypoint localization (percentage of correct keypoints [PCK] >70%). Methods: Retrospective technical validation of prospectively collected video from 14 PGY-1 interns at one academic center (July to August 2024). We annotated 203 frames (101 browser-based, 1280x720/854x480; 102 overhead, 3840x2160/1920x1080), yielding 6,232 ground-truth keypoints. An internally developed pipeline and MediaPipe Hands were evaluated. The primary endpoint was PCK normalized to the index-proximal bone; bounding-box-normalized PCK, detection rate, and per-region accuracy were also evaluated. Results: Primary PCK, normalized to a fixed anatomical hand scale, was 85.9% (95% CI, 80.3-91.0) for browser-based recordings and 81.5% (95% CI, 76.7-87.0) for overhead recordings. Secondary bounding-box-normalized PCK showed a similar pattern (91.6% vs 90.6%), and detection rates were high in both environments (94.9% vs 97.7%). In contrast, MediaPipe detection rates were only 5.3% for browser-based recordings and 15.4% for overhead recordings, resulting in substantially lower accuracy. Conclusion: Hand keypoint detection performance was comparable between browser-based and overhead recordings using the internally developed pipeline. These findings suggest that browser-based video acquisition can provide data of sufficient quality for ML-based hand keypoint detection, offering a scalable pathway for surgical skill assessment without specialized recording hardware.

after.authors: Moonga, J.; Soo, L.
after.abstract: Background Consumer electroencephalography (EEG)-based neurotechnologies are rapidly expanding across commercial digital health delivery networks and wellness markets. Positioned at the intersection of non-medical self-monitoring and clinical applications, these consumer devices introduce complex challenges for device governance and digital bioethics regarding product claims, data privacy, evidential substantiation, and user protection. Objective This qualitative study examined expert stakeholder perspectives on the ethical, regulatory, and data governance challenges of consumer EEG neurotechnology, focusing on the allocation of responsibility across product lifecycles. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with 19 expert stakeholders spanning research, clinical practice, engineering, industry, ethics, law, and regulatory policy across North America, Europe, and Latin America. Interview data were systematically analysed using reflexive thematic analysis to examine how governance challenges, evidence burdens, and responsibilities are conceptualized across the neurotechnology ecosystem. Results Five interrelated themes emerged: (1) Regulatory Category Boundaries and Oversight; (2) Evidential Credibility and Claims-Related Harm; (3) Neurodata Privacy, Security, and Inference; (4) Layered Governance and Explicit Accountability; and (5) Participation, Global Equity, and Contextual Responsiveness. Participants identified major friction in applying traditional medical oversight to nonmedical digital health uses, linked unverified claims to user vulnerability, and expressed concern over downstream neurodata processing. A connecting synthesis demonstrates that oversight responsibilities span multiple actors and development stages rather than resting on a single regulatory mechanism. Conclusions Effective governance of consumer EEG digital health devices requires explicit allocation of duties for claims substantiation, data practices, and user safety, backed by inclusive stakeholder participation and contextual responsiveness.

Interview data were systematically analysed using reflexive thematic analysis to examine how governance challenges, evidence burdens, and responsibilities are conceptualized across the neurotechnology ecosystem. Results Five interrelated themes emerged: (1) Regulatory Category Boundaries and Oversight; (2) Evidential Credibility and Claims-Related Harm; (3) Neurodata Privacy, Security, and Inference; (4) Layered Governance and Explicit Accountability; and (5) Participation, Global Equity, and Contextual Responsiveness. Participants identified major friction in applying traditional medical oversight to nonmedical digital health uses, linked unverified claims to user vulnerability, and expressed concern over downstream neurodata processing. A connecting synthesis demonstrates that oversight responsibilities span multiple actors and development stages rather than resting on a single regulatory mechanism. Conclusions Effective governance of consumer EEG digital health devices requires explicit allocation of duties for claims substantiation, data practices, and user safety, backed by inclusive stakeholder participation and contextual responsiveness.

after.authors: Mwandama, R.; Munthali, S.; Rahaman, M.; Zonda, J. M.; Gupta, R.; Mapila, S. A.
after.abstract: Background Postnatal care (PNC) is important for maternal and newborn health, but socioeconomic inequalities may limit timely access. In Malawi, evidence on PNC timing and the pathways linking household wealth to PNC is limited. We examined socioeconomic inequalities in timely PNC and whether antenatal care (ANC) and delivery-facility type accounted for part of the wealth gradient. Methodology We analysed 4,726 women with a live birth in the previous 24 months from the 2024 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey. PNC was timely when the first check occurred within two days of birth, delayed when it occurred later, and absent when no qualifying check was reported. Survey-weighted multinomial logistic regression examined associations between household wealth and PNC timing, with sequential adjustment for maternal education, ANC and place of delivery. The slope index of inequality (SII) and relative index of inequality (RII) summarised inequality. Pathway analyses examined ANC and delivery-facility type as mediators. Results Overall, 66.6% of women received timely PNC, 5.1% delayed PNC and 28.3% no PNC. Unadjusted, women in the richer and richest wealth quintiles had lower relative risk ratios (RRR) of no PNC than women in the poorest quintile (RRR 0.56 and 0.57, respectively). After full adjustment, the richer group remained less likely to have no PNC (RRR 0.67, 95% CI 0.50-0.89). Wealth inequality persisted (SII -8.4 percentage points, 95% CI -14.8 to -2.0; RII 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.93). Among all births, 26.6% of the wealth association with no PNC was accounted for by ANC and place of delivery, primarily home delivery. Conclusion Timely PNC remains unequally distributed by household wealth in Malawi. The findings suggest that reducing missed PNC opportunities requires attention to socioeconomic barriers and continuity from pregnancy through delivery and the postnatal period.

after.authors: Ahmed, H. M.; Owais, M.; Younas, N.
after.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular risk factors have changed in the United States, but trends in prevalence, management, and predicted risk through the post-pandemic period remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We analyzed 11 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) periods (1999-2000 through 2021-2023) among 60,199 nonpregnant adults aged 20 years. Survey-weighted regression assessed age-standardized trends, subgroup differences, and measurement-change sensitivity. We assessed awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes. PREVENT equations estimated 10- and 30-year risks among adults without self-reported cardiovascular disease (CVD). Results: Obesity increased from 47.4% to 57.2% (odds ratio [OR] per decade, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.16-1.30), with class III obesity more than doubling (4.7% to 9.7%). Diabetes increased from 8.2% to 12.7% (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.19-1.34), while current smoking declined from 24.4% to 14.9% (OR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.71-0.81). Hypertension, dyslipidemia, chronic kidney disease, and prior CVD showed no significant linear trends, although mean systolic blood pressure (BP) (124.2 to 120.2 mm Hg) and total cholesterol (203.6 to 188.1 mg/dL) declined, alongside improvements in other lipids. Hypertension and dyslipidemia awareness and treatment increased, but BP control peaked at 32.5% in 2013-2014 before declining to 21.5%, while LDL cholesterol control rose from 17.0% to 34.2%. Diabetes awareness increased, but treatment trends were nonsignificant. Glycemic control peaked at 51.2% in 2003-2004 before declining to 41.9% (P for nonlinearity <0.001). Predicted 10-year total CVD risk declined from 5.66% to 5.28%; atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) risk declined by 0.16 percentage points per decade (95% CI, 0.22 to 0.09), while heart failure (HF) risk increased by 0.10 (95% CI, 0.03-0.17). Their 2021-2023 estimates were nearly identical (3.20% and 3.19%, respectively); 30-year risks showed similar divergence. Conclusions: Improvements in smoking, blood pressure, and lipids coexisted with rising obesity and diabetes, declining blood pressure control after earlier gains, and divergent predicted ASCVD and HF risks.

after.authors: Pan, H.-C.; Chen, K.-H.; Tsai, C.-H.; Lin, Y.-H.; Wang, C.-Y.; Wu, V.-C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: College of Medicine, National Taiwan University
after.abstract: Background: Aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) and plasma renin activity (PRA) are measured at the screening stage of primary aldosteronism (PA) evaluation, but their prognostic relevance after confirmatory classification and subsequent treatment remains uncertain. Methods: We linked the seven-hospital Taiwan Primary Aldosteronism Investigation cohort (1991-2023) with nationwide health insurance and mortality data through June 2025. Patients were classified as confirmatory-test-defined essential hypertension (EH), PA without adrenalectomy, or PA with subsequent adrenalectomy. Covariate-adjusted Cox models evaluated screening logARR, logPRA, and logPAC separately in relation to incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or cardiovascular death). Results: Among 3,178 participants (EH, 1,433; PA without adrenalectomy, 834; PA with adrenalectomy, 911), 441 (13.9%) experienced MACE during a median 7.9-year follow-up. Adjusted hazard ratios (95% CIs) per 1-unit increase in logARR were 1.09 (1.00-1.19), 1.14 (1.03-1.26), and 0.95 (0.87-1.05), respectively; corresponding logPRA estimates were 0.91 (0.83-0.99), 0.87 (0.79-0.97), and 1.04 (0.93-1.16). LogPAC showed no consistent associations. Primary biomarker-by-phenotype interactions were not significant for logARR (P=0.057) or logPRA (P=0.069); time-varying adrenalectomy analyses were supportive but exploratory. Conclusions: Higher screening ARR and lower PRA were associated with subsequent MACE in confirmatory-test-defined EH and PA without adrenalectomy, but not clearly in PA with subsequent adrenalectomy.

after.authors: Eisenlohr-Moul, T. A.; Ross, A.; Peters, J. R.; Nagpal, A.; Schmalenberger, K.; Wiggs, K. K.; Knapp, E.; Patterson, A.; Martel, M.
after.abstract: Objective. Patients often describe menstrual-cycle worsening of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We prospectively evaluated sample- and person-level cycle effects on ADHD symptoms and their independence from cyclical negative affect and pain. Methods. In an intensive longitudinal cohort (2019-2024), 106 naturally cycling adults meeting DSM-5 ADHD criteria on integrated assessment rated daily inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity (Barkley Adult ADHD Rating Scale-IV), negative affect, and pain (median, 41 days) and provided daily salivary estradiol and progesterone for ovulation coding and phase-aligned cycle time (PACTS). Generalized additive models estimated sample-level and person-specific cycle curves; robust cyclicity was tested against each participant's own time-shuffle null. Lab cognitive testing at four counterbalanced phases provided post hoc validation. Results. Sample-average cycle effects were significant yet small (<1% of daily variance), but 54% of 87 participants tested individually were robustly cyclical in ADHD symptoms (95% CI, 44%-64%; inattention 43%, hyperactivity-impulsivity 26%), more often with informant-confirmed ADHD (69% vs 36%). Among them, the cycle explained median 52% and 51% of symptom variance, a mean swing of 2.6 and 2.1 DSM-5 criteria. Most remained cyclical after adjustment for affect (68%) or pain (81%). Worsening most often peaked at and after menses rather than premenstrually; no cycle met prospective criteria for premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Hormones did not differ by cyclicity. Conclusions. About half of these adults with ADHD showed robust cyclical symptom change, mostly not reducible to cyclical affect or pain and usually outside the premenstrual window. Future work should test its stability and whether a DSM-5 cyclical specifier is warranted.

after.authors: Hailemariam, M. D.; Sisaye, A. M. S.
after.abstract: Background: Population-based data on functional difficulty among school-age children in Ethiopia are scarce. The 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) included, for the first time, the UNICEF/Washington Group Child Functioning Module (CFM) for children aged 5-17 years. We estimated the prevalence and domain distribution of functional difficulty and associated factors in Ethiopia. Methods: We analysed cross-sectional EDHS data from 11,122 children aged 5-17 years (weighted n = 10,726) and 4,739 mothers. Functional difficulty was defined as "a lot of difficulty" or "cannot do at all" in any of 11 domains, or daily anxiety or depression. We estimated design-based prevalence and fitted multilevel logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) for any, non-affective and affective difficulty. Interviewer effects were examined with random-intercept models and within-cluster comparisons. Results: Overall, 9.5% (95% CI 8.1-11.1) of children had functional difficulty. Daily depression (6.8%) and anxiety (6.6%) dominated, and 70.3% of affected children had only affective difficulty. Difficulty in at least one non-affective domain affected 2.8% (2.2-3.7), with each domain at 0.5-1.4%. Prevalence ranged from 1.5% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 16.5% in Oromia Regional State. In adjusted models, children not attending school had higher odds of non-affective difficulty (AOR 2.82, 95% CI 2.01-3.96), and girls had lower odds (AOR 0.63, 0.48-0.84). Outcomes clustered strongly within families (sibling correlation 67.7%) and clusters (ICC 20.9%). Six of 163 interviewers (7.9% of the weighted sample) contributed 58.2% of weighted cases of daily anxiety or depression; in the same clusters they recorded daily symptoms for 56.4% of children, against 2.1% for other interviewers. Excluding 11 statistically outlying interviewers reduced the prevalence of any difficulty to 4.6% (3.6-5.8) and of daily anxiety or depression to 3.3%. The associations with school non-attendance and sex were unchanged. Conclusions: Functional difficulties across the sensory, physical, cognitive, and affective domains, including anxiety or depression, affect about 2-3% of Ethiopian children aged 5-17 years and are strongly associated with being out of school. Appropriate interventions and resource allocation should be considered.

after.authors: Reynolds, C.; Allen, R. J.; Fawcett, K. A.; Hollox, E. J.; Peljto, A.; Schwartz, D. A.; Wain, L. V.
after.abstract: Background: The MUC5B promoter variant (rs35705950) is the strongest common genetic risk factor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). MUC5B and MUC5AC contain variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions. Long-read sequencing resolves MUC5AC into three SNP-tagged haplogroups (H1, H2, H3) differing in repeat length, and MUC5B into two (H1, H2) differing in lineage but not length. The tags correlate with rs35705950, so whether a haplogroup effect is distinguishable from the promoter variant is unclear. Methods: We assigned MUC5AC and MUC5B haplogroups from imputed chromosome 11 array data in 771 European-ancestry IPF Job Exposures Study participants (385 cases, 386 controls). Logistic regression adjusted for age, smoking, principal components and centre, with and without rs35705950. The same models were fitted in TOPMed (1,961 cases, 3,816 controls). Results: MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 were each associated with IPF (H3 OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.26-2.09, p=1.8x10-4; MUC5B H1 OR 0.71, 0.52-0.98, p=0.038). Both attenuated on adjustment for rs35705950 (H3 OR 1.10, 0.83-1.45, p=0.52; MUC5B H1 OR 0.82, 0.58-1.15, p=0.25). A MUC5AC H2 association persisted after adjustment (OR 0.69, 0.51-0.94, p=0.017). In TOPMed the H3 findings replicated (unadjusted OR 1.62, 1.47-1.78, p<10-15; adjusted 0.94, 0.84-1.05, p=0.26), but the rs35705950-adjusted H2 association did not: the estimate was null overall (OR 0.99, 0.88-1.11, p=0.87) and in men and women separately (1.00, 0.87-1.16; 0.97, 0.79-1.19). The MUC5B tag failed quality control in TOPMed. Conclusions: The MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 associations are not independent of rs35705950. The MUC5AC H2 association seen here did not replicate. VNTR haplogroup does not appear to contribute to IPF risk independently of rs35705950.

In TOPMed the H3 findings replicated (unadjusted OR 1.62, 1.47-1.78, p<10-15; adjusted 0.94, 0.84-1.05, p=0.26), but the rs35705950-adjusted H2 association did not: the estimate was null overall (OR 0.99, 0.88-1.11, p=0.87) and in men and women separately (1.00, 0.87-1.16; 0.97, 0.79-1.19). The MUC5B tag failed quality control in TOPMed. Conclusions: The MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 associations are not independent of rs35705950. The MUC5AC H2 association seen here did not replicate. VNTR haplogroup does not appear to contribute to IPF risk independently of rs35705950.

items.title: Preprint: Assessing the Accuracy of the NeuroBooster Array for GBA1 Variant Detection
items.content_text: GBA1 variants are major Parkinson's disease risk factors, but their detection is challenging. We compared NeuroBooster Array (NBA) genotyping with reference sequencing in 3,744 individuals. NBA correctly identified 520/608 carriers (85.5%). Of 89 missed calls, 73 had no matching probe and 16 had missing calls. 25 participants had false positive calls. NBA should not be used alone for clinical decisions, but is very useful for case control analysis.
